params.body:
Version 0.4.0: a trend names the need it serves, and trends can reinforce or pull against each other.

- **`Trend.tags.drivers`** (`many`): the need a trend serves, one or two of the six drivers, the main one first. The Gentells pipeline writes it since 2026-09-28 (all 53 public trends), and the site shows it ("What they are after").
- **Two relations between trends,** symmetric, weight `asserted`:
  - `reinforces`: different behaviours, one larger movement, clearer together.
  - `pullsAgainst`: opposite directions on something that matters, a tension to build on.

  Both carry one sentence on what the two show together. They are judged, not counted: the pipeline keeps a link only when the judgement holds from both sides (49 of 105 proposed pairs on 2026-09-28). The concept-level `opposing` edges proved no substitute, because automatically named tensions tie unrelated trends together.
- **Added only,** so `tools/compat.mjs` reads every earlier release. The exports (SKOS/OWL) are regenerated. `CHANGELOG`, `package.json` and `VERSION.json` are at 0.4.0.

After merge: tag `v0.4.0`, then the pipeline pins it with `bin/sync-standard.mjs --ref v0.4.0`.

Checks: `npm test`, 50 of 50.
params.title: 0.4.0: trends name the need they serve, and reinforce or pull against each other
